subject: Mutual onramp: API keys, org & networking commitments
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cortexhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CortexHealth Evaluation — environment needs & timeline

Hi Stephanie / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and the dedicated routing options. We want to make sure the POC environment lines up with our SOC-sensitive workflows. Below are the items we need to confirm for the evaluation: 

- Org setup: ability to create tenant scoped orgs and control access to logs.
- API keys: ephemeral keys for test users + one long-lived service key for CI.
- IP allowlist: we will provide a short list of static egress ranges for our on-prem connectors.
- VPC peering: required for exchange of telemetry and to avoid public egress for PHI.

We have a tentative evaluation window the week of 2026-11-08, and procurement wants a clear mutual action plan and a decision close by 2026-11-30. Can you send a short MAP with who does what and dates? I attached a quick CSV of our internal network ranges.

Attach: cortex_requirements.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Senior Engineering Manager, Integrations
CortexHealth
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CortexHealth Evaluation — environment needs & timeline

Alex — thanks for the detail and the CSV. Appreciate the clarity on the PHI requirement. High-level MAP below (compact) so your procurement and security teams have concrete dates and owners. I’m including Ben (networking) and Rachel (security/compliance) to confirm specifics.

Mutual Onramp (compact) — Redwood | CortexHealth
- 2026-10-13: Redwood to propose org model & service-account pattern (owner: stephanie_nguyen)
- 2026-10-15: Ben to provide peering port map and peering prep checklist (owner: ben_carter)
- 2026-10-18: CortexHealth to confirm IP ranges + contact for network peering (owner: Alex)
- 2026-10-20: Redwood to provision sandbox org, seed API keys (ephemeral + service) and provide KMS integration notes (owner: rachel_kim)
- 2026-11-08: POC evaluation window begins
- 2026-11-22: Technical acceptance review and QA checklist signoff
- 2026-11-30: Commercial decision / close cadence

Attachments I'll send separately: a one-page MAP PDF you can share with Procurement. Ben / Rachel — can you confirm the peering approach below and any timing constraints? Also flag anything I missed for procurement (SLA items, retention, audit logs).

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cortexhealth.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CortexHealth Evaluation — environment needs & timeline

Quick technical notes / confirmations: 

- VPC peering: we can support AWS VPC peering in your target region; peering will be unidirectional for telemetry (redwood -> cortex) and we’ll provide an endpoint for return traffic where required. Typical turn-up lead time: 3 business days after both side’s terraform peering config and route table updates.
- IP allowlist: we need the CIDR blocks (one per region); Alex's CSV looks good — I see 3 ranges. Please confirm which ranges will be used for egress.
- API keys: we will generate two types in the sandbox: ephemeral user-scoped keys (TTL 12 hours) and one service key for your CI (rotatable via API). We’ll provide a quick script to rotate the service key during the POC.
- KMS / key management: Rachel will follow up on KMS/HSM integration notes.

Action items for CortexHealth network team: share exact CIDRs + contact for peering (tombstone: 2026-10-18). Once we have that, I’ll open the peering request and send the terraform snippet you can apply on your side.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
